text:
ACME Corp - Jane: Hey — after the weekend deploy our app hitting the Redwood Dedicated pool is intermittently returning 500s and very high tail latencies (several 10s of seconds). A few request IDs: req_9f3b2a4e, req_c1d5f8a7, req_7b0e2c11. Customers see failures ~1-2% of requests, more during bursts.
Maya (Support): Sorry you're seeing that. Can you paste a curl you use so we can repro? Also which pool/region is this against?
ACME Corp - Jane: Using reserved-pool eu-west-2: pool-id rp-eu-42. Curl we use locally: 
```bash
curl -s -D - \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":512}' \n  https://api.redwood-inference.eu/v1/generate?tenant=acme
```
Maya (Support): Thanks. Can you run that with --trace or add X-Request-Id header to force a stable ID so we can match server logs? Example header we prefer: `X-RW-Req: acme-test-01`.
ACME Corp - Jane: added header and reran once, got 500. Full curl: 
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-RW-Req: acme-test-01" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n-d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"test","max_tokens":32}' \nhttps://api.redwood-inference.eu/v1/generate?tenant=acme
```
Maya (Support): Passing this to infra/SRE to fetch logs for those req ids and pool rp-eu-42. @Jorge any quick insight?
Jorge (SRE): I'll pull logs. Can the customer also run `kubectl get pods -n dedicated-rp-eu-42` and paste pod names? If we can match pod & node for the reqs, we can request debug bundle.
ACME Corp - Jane: pod list snippet: 
```
NAME                                        READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
serve-rw-large-0                            1/1     Running   0          3d
serve-rw-large-1                            1/1     Running   0          2d
serve-gateway-0                             2/2     Running   1          7d
proxy-reserved-rp-eu-42-6f9c7              1/1     Running   4          12h
```
Jorge (SRE): Noted. The proxy pod restarts are interesting (4 restarts). Can you `kubectl logs proxy-reserved-rp-eu-42-6f9c7 --since=2h -n dedicated-rp-eu-42` and paste any 500-related traces?
ACME Corp - Jane: Logs show short stack traces around connection reset and a code path: `error=allocation_failed: burst_capacity_exhausted` and `route: serve-rw-large-1`. Snippet: 
```
2024-06-12T09:14:22Z ERROR alloc: failed to acquire slot: allocation_failed: burst_capacity_exhausted (pool=rp-eu-42)
2024-06-12T09:14:22Z WARN  gateway: upstream returned 500 for req acme-test-01
```
Anika (Infra): That allocation_failed string suggests our autoscaler hit the cap and returned immediate errors rather than queueing. We need node-level metrics from the GPU nodes at that time: nvidia-smi, dmesg, and kubelet logs. I can assemble a debug bundle if SRE requests it.
Jorge (SRE): Yes please collect a debug bundle for the node where serve-rw-large-1 was scheduled. Commands I usually ask customers to run (if they can ssh into node): 
```bash
sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2h ago" > kubelet.log
sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > dmesg.txt
nvidia-smi -q -d UTILIZATION,POWER,TEMPERATURE > nvidia.txt
kubectl logs serve-rw-large-1 -n dedicated-rp-eu-42 --since=2h > pod.log
```
Maya (Support): If you can't ssh, we can ask infra to pull node diagnostics from the cloud provider and attach. Also please include `kubectl describe pod serve-rw-large-1 -n dedicated-rp-eu-42` output.
ACME Corp - Jane: We don't have node ssh rights (managed reserved). I'll collect the pod logs and describe and run the curl in a loop to reproduce. Attaching pod.describe and pod.log excerpts: 
```
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  3d    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned .../serve-rw-large-1 to node-gpu-17
  Warning Failed     2h    kubelet            Error: failed to allocate device plugins: allocation_failed
```
pod.log shows repeated OOM_kill marks around the runtime when a large burst arrives.
Jorge (SRE): OOM_kill on GPU processes plus allocation_failed — possible memory fragmentation or driver issue. I'll open an infra debug request to collect the node-level logs and nvidia driver logs. @Anika can you escalate to cloud ops for node-gpu-17?
Anika (Infra): On it. I'll request a cloud-side snapshot and the node diagnostic bundle (dmesg, system journal, driver logs) and add it to this thread when ready. Request ID to infra: infra-bundle-7711.
debug-bot: New debug request created: infra-bundle-7711. Please allow ~15-30m for data aggregation.
Maya (Support): Thanks. In parallel, can ACME try a short mitigation: set request concurrency hint lower or add client-side retry with exponential backoff to reduce instant burst? Also if you can run the curl test with `X-RW-Req` headers for 10 runs and paste request IDs, that'll help map failures.
ACME Corp - Jane: Will do. I'll run 20 sequential curls with X-RW-Req: acme-burst-01..20 and post the IDs. Thanks all.
Jorge (SRE): Once infra bundle attached I'll grep for `allocation_failed`, kernel OOM messages, and NV driver XID errors. If we confirm driver XID or GPU reset, we'll schedule a node drain + repro on a patch kernel/driver.
Anika (Infra): Debug bundle attached: https://internal-blobstore/redwood/debug/infra-bundle-7711.tar.gz (internal link). Contains nvidia-smi logs showing GPU retention but occasional GPU reset events at 09:14 and 09:15, plus kernel logs with a GPU UVM abort.
Maya (Support): Got it. We'll review and follow up with a recommended rollback or targeted node patch. Keeping thread open for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
